evidence.quote: Each piece can only be used once on the turn they are purchased, and its strength cannot be split among more than one purpose.
If the newly-exhausted pieces do not equal the strength of the Crisis, the Crisis succeeds.
evidence.interpretation: This literal published wording alone is not treated as independent verification of >=. The exact human override resolves the adopted comparison.

evidence.quote: Just accept my answer. You can note it as my interpretation.
The Crisis fails when the strength of newly exhausted defense pieces is equal to or greater than attacking strength.

If the Commander is vacant, Military Affairs will act in its stead (choosing which pieces to exhaust etc.) If that office is also vacant, the Chairman will choose. The player acting as Commander will not lose or gain trophies.

When it comes to the unrest cubes, they shouldn't count for Foreign Invasions. This means they don't add to strength of the attack and they don't inform the number of tower levels that might be placed in the region if it is not defended.

evidence.source: Rules p37, Firms in Final Scoring
evidence.quote: Then, regardless of Company success or failure, shareholders may perform one special retirement before proceeding with the rest of Final Scoring.
